30270-that-mother-in-law-of-mine.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. t is, if Bessie had only been an orphan. But there was her mother, who had joined us on our summer trip, after the first two weeks of unalloyed happiness, and threatened to accompany us through life. Already it almost made the prospect dismal. The idea that Bessie and I would ever quarrel, or even have any impatient words together, had seemed to me to be simply ridiculous.

56673-vagabonding-down-the-andes-being-t.title: Aires
56673-vagabonding-down-the-andes-being-t.creator: Harry A. Franck
56673-vagabonding-down-the-andes-being-t.description: A book by Harry A. Franck. f the Incas from Quito to Cuzco. Every traveler, however, knows the tendency of a journey to grow under one’s feet. This one grew with such tropical luxuriance that before it ended I had spent, not eight months, but four full years, and had covered not merely the ancient Inca Empire, but all the ten republics and three colonies of South America.

arxiv-2209-13709.title: A new reduced order model of imcompressible Stokes equations
arxiv-2209-13709.creator: Yangwen Zhang
arxiv-2209-13709.description: Abstract In this paper we propose a new reduced order model (ROM) to the imcompressible Stokes equations. Numerical experiments show that our ROM is accurate and efficient. Under some assumptions on the problem data, we prove that the convergence rates of the new ROM is the same with standard solvers.

arxiv-2302-01582.title: Controlling for Stereotypes in Multimodal Language Model Evaluation
arxiv-2302-01582.creator: Manuj Malik Richard Johansson
arxiv-2302-01582.description: Abstract We propose a methodology and design two benchmark sets for measuring to what extent language-and-vision language models use the visual signal in the presence or absence of stereotypes. The first benchmark is designed to test for stereotypical colors of common objects, while the second benchmark considers gender stereotypes.

arxiv-2307-08140.title: GastroVision: A Multi-class Endoscopy Image Dataset for Computer Aided Gastrointestinal Disease Detection
arxiv-2307-08140.creator: Debesh Jha ∗, Vanshali Sharma ∗, Neethi Dasu, Nikhil Kumar Tomar, Steven Hicks, M.K. Bhuyan, Pradip K. Das, Michael A. Riegler, Pål Halvorsen, Ulas Bagci † {\dagger}, Thomas de Lange † {\dagger}
arxiv-2307-08140.description: Abstract Integrating real-time artificial intelligence (AI) systems in clinical practices faces challenges such as scalability and acceptance. These challenges include data availability, biased outcomes, data quality, lack of transparency, and underperformance on unseen datasets from different distributions. The scarcity of large-scale, precisely labeled, and diverse datasets are the major challenge for clinical integration.

arxiv-2308-10357.title: An Explicit Fourth-Order Hybrid-Variable Method for Euler Equations with A Residual-Consistent Viscosity
arxiv-2308-10357.creator: Xianyi Zeng
arxiv-2308-10357.description: Abstract . In this paper we present a formally fourth-order accurate hybrid-variable method for the Euler equations in the context of method of lines. The hybrid-variable (HV) method seeks numerical approximations to both cell-averages and nodal solutions and evolves them in time simultaneously; and it is proved in previous work that these methods are inherent superconvergent.

arxiv-2309-07240.title: Eulerian Polynomials for Digraphs
arxiv-2309-07240.creator: Kyle Celano, Nicholas Sieger, Sam Spiro
arxiv-2309-07240.description: Abstract Given an n n -vertex digraph D D and a labeling σ : V ⁡ ( D ) → [ n ] \sigma\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}V(D)\to[n] , we say that an arc u → v u\to v of D D is a descent of σ \sigma if σ ⁡ ( u ) > σ ⁡ ( v ) \sigma(u)>\sigma(v) .

arxiv-2311-15046.title: CERN-TH-2023-210 Nonperturbative running of the tensor operator for N f = 3 N_{\mathrm{\scriptstyle f}}=3 QCD from the chirally rotated Schrödinger Functional
arxiv-2311-15046.creator: Isabel Campos Plasencia, Mattia Dalla Brida, Giulia Maria de Divitiis, Andrew Lytle, Mauro Papinutto, Ludovica Pirelli, Anastassios Vladikas
arxiv-2311-15046.description: Abstract We study the Renormalisation Group (RG) running of the non-singlet tensor operator, for N f = 3 N_{\mathrm{\scriptstyle f}}=3 QCD with Wilson fermions in a mixed action setup, with standard Schrödinger Functional (SF) boundary conditions for sea quarks and chirally rotated Schrödinger Functional ( χ \chi SF) boundary conditions for valence quarks.

arxiv-2408-13647.title: Synthetic Networks That Preserve Edge Connectivity
arxiv-2408-13647.creator: Lahari Anne 1 [0009-0007-5708-2405], The-Anh Vu-Le 1 [0000-0002-4480-5535], Minhyuk Park 1 [0000-0002-8676-7565], Tandy Warnow 1 [0000-0001-7717-3514], George Chacko 1 [0000-0002-2127-1892]
arxiv-2408-13647.description: Abstract Since true communities within real-world networks are rarely known, synthetic networks with planted ground truths are valuable for evaluating the performance of community detection methods. Of the synthetic network generation tools available, Stochastic Block Models (SBMs) produce networks with ground truth clusters that well approximate input parameters from real-world networks and clusterings.

arxiv-2411-03778.title: Topology and dynamics of a flow that has a non-saddle set or a W W -set Thanks: The authors are funded by the Spanish Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación through grant PGC2018-098321-B-I00 and, for the second author, also grant RYC2018-025843-I
arxiv-2411-03778.creator: H. Barge, J.J. Sánchez-Gabites, J.M.R. Sanjurjo
arxiv-2411-03778.description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to study dynamical and topological properties of a flow in the region of influence of an isolated non-saddle set or a W W -set in a manifold. These are certain classes of compact invariant sets in whose vicinity the asymptotic behaviour of the flow is somewhat controlled.

arxiv-2508-18719.title: Globally Stable Discrete Time PID Passivity-based Control of Power Converters: Simulation and Experimental Results
arxiv-2508-18719.creator: Alessio Moreschini, Wei He, Romeo Ortega, Yiheng Lu, Tao Li
arxiv-2508-18719.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alessio Moreschini, Wei He, Romeo Ortega, Yiheng Lu, Tao Li. The key idea behind PID Passivity-based Control (PID-PBC) is to leverage the passivity property of PIDs (for all positive gains) and wrap the PID controller around a passive output to ensure global stability in closed-loop.

arxiv-2510-17771.title: Seeing but Not Believing: Probing the Disconnect Between Visual Attention and Answer Correctness in VLMs
arxiv-2510-17771.creator: Zhining Liu, Ziyi Chen, Hui Liu, Chen Luo, Xianfeng Tang, Suhang Wang, Joy Zeng, Zhenwei Dai, Zhan Shi, Tianxin Wei, Benoit Dumoulin, Hanghang Tong
arxiv-2510-17771.description: Abstract Vision-Language Models (VLMs) achieve strong results on multimodal tasks such as visual question answering, yet they can still fail even when the correct visual evidence is present. In this work, we systematically investigate whether these failures arise from not perceiving the evidence or from not leveraging it effectively.

arxiv-2511-05320.title: What Are the Facts? Automated Extraction of Court-Established Facts from Criminal-Court Opinions
arxiv-2511-05320.creator: Klára Bendová, Tomáš Knap, Jan Černý, Vojtěch Pour, Jaromir Savelka, Ivana Kvapilíková, Jakub Drápal
arxiv-2511-05320.description: Abstract Criminal justice administrative data contain only a limited amount of information about the committed offense. There is, however, an unused source of extensive information in continental European courts‘ decisions: Descriptions of criminal behaviors in verdicts by which offenders are found guilty.

arxiv-2511-08114.title: Introducing Nylon Face Mask Attacks: A Dataset for Evaluating Generalised Face Presentation Attack Detection
arxiv-2511-08114.creator: Manasa ∗ , Sushrut Patwardhan ‡ , Narayan Vetrekar † , Pavan Kumar ∗ , R. S. Gad † , Raghavendra Ramachandra ‡
arxiv-2511-08114.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manasa ∗ , Sushrut Patwardhan ‡ , Narayan Vetrekar † , Pavan Kumar ∗ , R. S. Gad † , Raghavendra Ramachandra ‡. Face recognition systems are increasingly deployed across a wide range of applications, including smartphone authentication, access control, and border security. However, these systems remain vulnerable to presentation attacks (PAs), which can significantly compromise their reliability.

We sought to estimate treatment outcomes and identify risk factors associated with poor outcomes in patients with MDRTB. Methodology/pr

pmc-11431044.title: Real-World Treatment Patterns, Sequencing, and Outcomes in Patients with Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma Receiving Avelumab First-Line Maintenance in the United States
pmc-11431044.creator: Helen H Moon, Mairead Kearney, Seyed Hamidreza Mahmoudpour, Chiemeka Ike, Valerie Morris, Andrew Rava, Sonia Kim, Haiyan Sun, Marley Boyd, Gabriel Gomez Rey
pmc-11431044.description: For patients with locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), first-line (1L) treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy (PBC) followed by avelumab 1L maintenance (1LM) is a recommended therapy per treatment guidelines in patients without disease progression. However, contemporary real-world (rw) data among patients receiving this treatment are necessary to understand clinical outcomes and optimal treatment sequencing.

pmc-11515777.title: Exploring the link between dietary zinc intake and endometriosis risk: insights from a cross-sectional analysis of American women
pmc-11515777.creator: Yingmei Huang, Yumei Wei, Feng Liang, Yingqin Huang, Jianyong Huang, Xuehui Luo, Baoli Xie
pmc-11515777.description: BackgroundEndometriosis is a complex disorder with genetic, immune, inflammatory, and multifactorial etiologies. Zinc, an essential trace element, plays a crucial role in various physiological processes. Dysregulation or deficiency of zinc can lead to aberrations in human physiology. However, the association between dietary zinc and endometriosis remains ambiguous. This study aimed to investigate the link between dietary zinc intake and endometriosis.

pmc-11584353.title: Endoscopic Treatment of Scaphocephaly: A Case Study
pmc-11584353.creator: Virginie Lafontaine, Florian Le Lann, Laurane Benoit, Jean Philippe Giot, Béatrice Morand
pmc-11584353.description: Craniosynostosis is a congenital craniofacial anomaly caused by the premature closure of one or more sutures. Scaphocephaly is the most common form. Endoscopic surgery is increasingly being used for the treatment of a single synostosis. We present our first case of endoscopy-assisted surgery for scaphocephaly in a three-month-old baby. Follow-up at one year was satisfactory, showing a good aesthetic result.

pmc-13248963.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Biofire FilmArray Blood Culture Identification 2 (BCID2) for Bloodstream Infections in Limpopo, South Africa
pmc-13248963.creator: Nhlayiso Atalia Maswanganyi, Kabelo Gabriel Kaapu, Molebogeng Ruth Lekalakala-Mokaba, Ivy Rukasha
pmc-13248963.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBloodstream infections are a leading global cause of mortality and morbidity. Timely and accurate diagnosis improves outcomes, especially in resource-limited settings. Rapid and accurate diagnostic tools are essential for effective treatment, particularly in resource-limited settings.

pmc-13270025.title: Systematic optimization of PD-L1 and CLDN18.2 CAR-T designs identifies a bicistronic dual-target, double-CD3ζ architecture with enhanced antitumor activity in gastric cancer
pmc-13270025.creator: Xiang Zhang, Yao-jie Kong, Jing-yao Li, Heng-hui Li, Liang Chen
pmc-13270025.description: BackgroundGastric cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with limited efficacy of immunotherapies due to intratumoral heterogeneity, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and antigen-loss escape. The optimization of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy targeting PD-L1 and Claudin18.2 (CLDN18.2) is crucial for improving the antitumor response.MethodsWe performed a stepwise optimization of CAR designs targeting PD-L1 and CLDN18.

pmc-13464578.title: Metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming via the PLOD1–PFKP axis drives cisplatin resistance in HNSCC
pmc-13464578.creator: Xinyuan Zhao, Xin Liao, Yunfan Lin, Xu Chen, Pei Lin, Ye Lu, Jiarong Zheng, Meiyan Zou, Bing Guo, Li Cui
pmc-13464578.description: Cisplatin remains a cornerstone of treatment for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet its therapeutic efficacy is often undermined by acquired resistance. Here, we identify the PLOD1–PFKP–glycolysis axis as a central driver of cisplatin resistance. PLOD1 is significantly upregulated in cisplatin-resistant tumors and correlates with poor prognosis.

pmc-13519775.title: Oseltamivir drug‐disease modelling in infants with influenza virus infection
pmc-13519775.creator: Kun Wang, David W Kimberlin, Richard J Whitley, Edward P Acosta, For the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Collaborative Antiviral Study Group
pmc-13519775.description: AimsOseltamivir is a commonly used neuraminidase inhibitor for treatment of influenza infection, but little data exist regarding concentration‐response relationships.MethodsPharmacokinetic (PK) and viral dynamic data from an earlier NIAID Collaborative Antiviral Study Group trial in paediatric patients with influenza from 0–23 months of age were used to create a PK model linked to an influenza viral dynamic model.

pmc-13631314.description: Skeletal muscle hypertrophy is a hallmark of resistance training that improves health and longevity.
